summary: The root سأم (sAm) primarily conveys the meaning of being weary, tired, or bored with something. It implies a state of being fed up or disgusted, leading to a cessation of desire or effort.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: سَئِمَ مِنْهُ , (S, M, Msb, K,) and سَئِمَهُ, (M, Msb, K,) aor. سَأََ, (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. سَأَمٌ (S, M, K) and سَأْمٌ (K) and سَأَمَةٌ (S, M) and سَآمٌ and سَآمَةٌ, (S, Msb, K,) He turned away with disgust from it; was averse from it; was disgusted at it or with it; loathed, or nauseated, it; (S, M, Msb, K;) namely, a thing; (S, M, K;) syn. مَلَّ, (S, M, Msb, K,) and ضَجِرَ: (Msb:) سَآمَةٌ exceeds مَلَالٌ. (Ham pp. 775-6.) It is said in the Kur [xli.
He, or it, made him to turn away with disgust, to be averse, to be disgusted, to loathe, or to nauseate. (M, K.)

an [intensive] epithet from 1 [meaning Wont, or much disposed, to turn away with disgust, to be averse, to be disgusted, to loathe, or to nauseate ]: (S, M, K:) or much affected with vexation, or disgust; having little patience. (Ham p. 532.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
